--- title: "Retail Site Selection & Catchment Analysis for a New C-Store with Click & Collect in Liverpool" description: "Multi-criteria GIS site selection and network catchment modelling in Python to identify the optimal location for a new Marks & Spencer convenience store and Click & Collect facility in Liverpool." date: "2023-12-15" image: retail_site.svg categories: [Python, Spatial Analysis, Retail Analytics, Network Analysis] lightbox: true --- ## Executive Summary & Retail Location Problem The rapid growth of e-commerce and hybrid **Click & Collect (C&C)** grocery fulfilment has transformed urban retail location strategy. Rather than relying solely on large out-of-town superstores, major UK grocery retailers increasingly deploy neighbourhood **convenience stores (`c-stores`) equipped with Click & Collect facilities** to capture time-poor commuters, small urban households, and digitally engaged neighbourhoods. In this assignment, we conduct a multi-stage GIS site-selection analysis across **Liverpool (`E08000012`, 298 LSOAs)** to identify the **optimal location for a new Marks & Spencer (M&S) convenience store with a Click & Collect (C&C) facility**. Originally developed across **QGIS**, **ArcGIS Pro (Network Analyst)**, and **R**, the entire spatial workflow and cartographic output series (`map1` through `map6`) are reproduced here directly from the underlying shapefiles in Python. --- ## Three-Stage Site Selection Methodology The site-selection model integrates **Demand-Side Socio-Demographics** and **Supply-Side Retail Competition** across three sequential filtering stages: ```{mermaid} %%{init: { 'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': { 'primaryColor': '#fff3bf', 'primaryTextColor': '#1a1a1a', 'primaryBorderColor': '#f59f00', 'lineColor': '#495057', 'secondaryColor': '#fff9db', 'tertiaryColor': '#fef9e7', 'clusterBkg': '#fffdf0', 'clusterBorder': '#fab005', 'fontFamily': 'inherit', 'fontSize': '14px' } }}%% flowchart TD subgraph Input["Input Spatial Datasets (EPSG:27700)"] D["Demand Data

• 1–2 Person Household Density (Census 2011 QS406EW)"] S["Supply Data
• Geolytix Foodstores 2023 Retail Points
• 68 Existing Convenience Stores (C-Stores)
• 2 Supermarkets with C&C (Tesco & Sainsbury's)

Every ESRI Shapefile (`.shp`) is accompanied by its complete set of 6 files (`.shp` geometry, `.shx` positional index, `.dbf` attribute table, `.prj` coordinate system WKT, `.cpg` encoding, and `.qmd` QGIS metadata), alongside the GeoPackage `RetailCentres_Liverpool.gpkg`. ::: {#8d3a7327 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import os import glob import warnings warnings.filterwarnings("ignore") import numpy as np import pandas as pd import geopandas as gpd import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import matplotlib.patches as mpatches import matplotlib.lines as mlines import matplotlib.patheffects as pe from matplotlib.colors import ListedColormap, BoundaryNorm # Robust data directory resolution across document, project root, and absolute paths data_candidates = [ os.path.normpath(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "../../../data/data_python/retail_site_select")), os.path.normpath(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "data/data_python/retail_site_select")), "/Users/jay/Desktop/websiteV02/data/data_python/retail_site_select" ] DATA_DIR = next((d for d in data_candidates if os.path.exists(d)), data_candidates[0]) if os.path.exists(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, "data")): DATA_DIR = os.path.join(DATA_DIR, "data") # Inventory all 17 shapefiles in data/data_python/retail_site_select/ and verify their 6 companion files shp_inventory = [] for shp_path in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, "**/*.shp"), recursive=True)): base = os.path.splitext(shp_path)[0] exts = sorted([os.path.splitext(f)[1] for f in glob.glob(base + ".*")]) gdf_tmp = gpd.read_file(shp_path) shp_inventory.append({ "Layer Name": os.path.basename(base), "Subfolder": os.path.relpath(os.path.dirname(shp_path), DATA_DIR), "Features": len(gdf_tmp), "Geometry": gdf_tmp.geom_type.unique()[0], "CRS": str(gdf_tmp.crs), "Files": f"{len(exts)} ({', '.join(exts)})" }) pd.DataFrame(shp_inventory) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

Grocery Shopping Prevalence Across Liverpool LSOAs (`IUC 2018`) The Consumer Data Research Centre (CDRC) **2018 Internet User Classification (`IUC 2018`)** segments Great Britain neighbourhoods into 10 distinct digital engagement profiles using Small Area Estimation (SAE) and gradient-boosted decision trees trained on British Population Survey (BPS) online shopping transactions, Ofcom broadband infrastructure, and ONS Census demographics. Based on each IUC group's *Buy Groceries Online* propensity $z$-score in the CDRC User Guide, Liverpool's 298 LSOAs are classified into four ordinal **Online Grocery Shopping Prevalence** tiers (`OrdinalTes`): * **High Prevalence (`4`, Blue Hatching `///`):** *e-Cultural Creators* (`GRP 1`, $z = +1.6$), *e-Professionals* (`GRP 2`, $z = +1.4$), *e-Veterans* (`GRP 3`, $z = +0.9$), and *e-Rational Utilitarians* (`GRP 5`, $z = +0.65$) — $61$ LSOAs ($20.5\%$). * **Moderate Prevalence (`3`, Green Hatching `///`):** *e-Mainstream* (`GRP 6`, $z = +0.05$) — $38$ LSOAs ($12.8\%$). * **Low Prevalence (`2`, Orange Hatching `///`):** *Digital Seniors* (`GRP 8`, $z = -0.10$) and *Settled Offline Communities* (`GRP 9`, $z = -0.35$) — $8$ LSOAs ($2.7\%$). * **Very Low Prevalence (`1`, Red Hatching `///`):** *Youthful Urban Fringe* (`GRP 4`, $z = -0.45$), *Passive and Uncommitted Users* (`GRP 7`, $z = -0.45$), and *e-Withdrawn* (`GRP 10`, $z = -1.60$) — $191$ LSOAs ($64.1\%$). ::: {#a45fd590 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10.5, 12.5), dpi=150) # Base Liverpool LSOA fill liv_bound.plot(ax=ax, facecolor="#f2f2f2", edgecolor="#4a4a4a", linewidth=1.2, zorder=1) # Plot each Online Grocery Shopping Prevalence category with coloured diagonal hatching matching map1.png prevalence_styles = [ (4, "High Prevalence", "#1f78b4", "#deebf7"), (3, "Moderate Prevalence", "#74c476", "#e5f5e0"), (2, "Low Prevalence", "#fdae6b", "#feedde"), (1, "Very Low Prevalence", "#e31a1c", "#fee5d9"), ] for code, label, edge_col, fill_col in prevalence_styles: sub = iuc_liv[iuc_liv["OrdinalTes"] == code] sub.plot( ax=ax, facecolor=fill_col, edgecolor=edge_col, hatch="///", linewidth=0.6, alpha=0.85, zorder=3 ) liv_bound.boundary.plot(ax=ax, color="#333333", linewidth=1.3, zorder=5) plot_retail_centres(ax, black_outline=False) add_uk_inset_liv(fig, pos=[0.08, 0.73, 0.19, 0.20]) add_north_arrow(ax, x=0.88, y=0.88) add_tick_scale_bar(ax, x0=342500, y0=381200) # Build exact legend matching map1.png leg_handles = [ mpatches.Patch(facecolor=fill_col, edgecolor=edge_col, hatch="///", label=label) for _, label, edge_col, fill_col in prevalence_styles ] leg_handles.extend([ mpatches.Patch(facecolor="none", edgecolor="none", label=""), mlines.Line2D([], [], color="white", marker="o", markeredgecolor="#7f7f7f", markersize=8, linestyle="None", label="Retail Centres in Liverpool"), mpatches.Patch(facecolor="#e5e5e5", edgecolor="#7f7f7f", label="Liverpool Boundary") ]) leg = ax.legend( handles=leg_handles, title="Online Grocery Shopping Prevalence", loc="lower left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.02, 0.01), frameon=False, fontsize=10, title_fontsize=11 ) leg._legend_box.align = "left" ax.set_xlim(331800, 346500) ax.set_ylim(379500, 398500) ax.set_axis_off() fig.text(0.5, 0.005, "Source: CDRC IUC 2018; CDRC Retail Centre Boundaries (Previous Versions); ONS Geography, LAD (May 2020) Boundaries UK BFE.", ha="center", fontsize=8) plt.tight_layout() plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/cell-4-output-1.png){width=1445 height=1877} ::: ::: --- ### Map 2: Overlaying Deprivation (`IMD 2019`) with Online Grocery Shopping Prevalence A new Marks & Spencer C-Store with Click & Collect requires a catchment that is not only digitally engaged (`High Prevalence`) but also economically affluent enough to sustain premium convenience expenditure. In Map 2, we classify the **English Index of Multiple Deprivation (`IMD 2019`) Rank** across Liverpool (`1` = most deprived in England, `32,844` = least deprived) into three tiers: 1. **More Deprived (`Rank 10 – 1,416`, Solid Red):** Severely deprived neighbourhoods concentrated in north Liverpool (*Kirkdale*, *Everton*, *Anfield*, *Walton*) and outer social housing estates (*Speke*, *Norris Green*). 2. **Moderate (`Rank 1,416 – 15,000`, Salmon Pink):** Transitional middle-income urban neighbourhoods. 3. **More Affluent (`Rank 15,000 – 31,562`, White):** Affluent suburban and waterfront neighbourhoods (*Allerton Road*, *Mossley Hill*, *Childwall*, *Woolton*, *Wavertree*, and *Liverpool City Centre Waterfront*). Overlaying the hatched `Online Grocery Shopping Prevalence` layer reveals a striking spatial inverse correlation: **High Online Grocery Shopping Prevalence (blue hatching over white/pink background) clusters tightly in south-central and central Liverpool** around the **Allerton Road**, **Smithdown Road**, **Woolton**, and **City Centre** corridors, as well as an affluent pocket north of **Old Swan**. ::: {#704ed3e2 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10.5, 12.5), dpi=150) # 1. Overlay hatched Online Grocery Shopping Prevalence (transparent fill so IMD colours show through!) for code, label, edge_col, _ in prevalence_styles: sub = iuc_liv[iuc_liv["OrdinalTes"] == code] sub.plot( ax=ax, facecolor="none", edgecolor=edge_col, hatch="///", linewidth=0.65, zorder=3 ) liv_bound.boundary.plot(ax=ax, color="#333333", linewidth=1.3, zorder=5) plot_retail_centres(ax, black_outline=True) add_uk_inset_liv(fig, pos=[0.08, 0.73, 0.19, 0.20]) add_north_arrow(ax, x=0.88, y=0.88) add_tick_scale_bar(ax, x0=342500, y0=381200) leg_handles_m2 = [ mpatches.Patch(facecolor="#ff0000", edgecolor="black", label="More Deprived (10 - 1416)"), mpatches.Patch(facecolor="#fcae91", edgecolor="black", label="Moderate (1416 - 15000)"), mpatches.Patch(facecolor="#ffffff", edgecolor="black", label="More Affluent (15000 - 31562)"), mpatches.Patch(facecolor="none", edgecolor="none", label=""), mpatches.Patch(facecolor="none", edgecolor="#1f78b4", hatch="///", label="High Prevalence"), mpatches.Patch(facecolor="none", edgecolor="#74c476", hatch="///", label="Moderate Prevalence"), mpatches.Patch(facecolor="none", edgecolor="#fdae6b", hatch="///", label="Low Prevalence"), mpatches.Patch(facecolor="none", edgecolor="#e31a1c", hatch="///", label="Very Low Prevalence"), mpatches.Patch(facecolor="none", edgecolor="none", label=""), mlines.Line2D([], [], color="white", marker="o", markeredgecolor="black", markersize=8, linestyle="None", label="Retail Centres in Liverpool"), ] leg = ax.legend( handles=leg_handles_m2, title="IMD2019 Rank & Online Grocery Shopping Prevalence", loc="lower left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.02, 0.01), frameon=False, fontsize=9.5, title_fontsize=10.5 ) leg._legend_box.align = "left" ax.set_xlim(331800, 346500) ax.set_ylim(379500, 398500) ax.set_axis_off() fig.text(0.5, 0.005, "Source: CDRC IMD 2019;
